author: Ash

copy.intro: You want a heavy silver ring with a skull or a cross on it, and Chrome Hearts won't sell you one online. Its web shop stops at underwear, scents and Baccarat crystal, so its jewelry means a trip to one of its boutiques. Here are nine silver makers that do sell rings online and ship to the US. The biker and rock'n'roll houses come first, the sculptors last.

bodies.bill-wall-leather:
Bill Wall Leather is the pick for carved biker silver with real history behind it, and the Double Skull Ring ($216) is a good first piece. It's an open ring, shaped to your size and adjustable later.

Bill Wall started the brand in Malibu in 1985, sewing his own leather riding gear after a motorcycle crash. He still carves each original out of a block of silver, then casts it in small numbers, and most pieces are made to order. Rings start at $166, and the top of the range is custom gold and pavé work past $40,000.

There's no Bill Wall store to try anything on. To hold a ring before you buy, go to The Great Frog's shops in New York or LA.
bodies.the-great-frog:
The Great Frog is the one to choose if you want skull rings from a shop you can walk into. It's been making rock'n'roll jewelry in London since 1972, and it has US stores on Orchard Street in New York and Melrose Avenue in LA. The Small Skull Ring (£145, about $193) is where to start.

Online, prices are in pounds, and duties and taxes are charged at checkout. So the total you see is the total you pay, with no bill at the door. The Skull & Crossbones Ring (£235, about $312) is made to order in sterling silver, and handmade pieces take about a week before they're posted.

Sizes are UK letters, from F½ to Z+1, so check yours first. Online jewelry can't be exchanged. A wrong size means a refund within 28 days and a fresh order.
bodies.hard-jewelry:
Hard Jewelry is where to start if Chrome Hearts prices are the problem. Most of its gothic rings come in stainless steel or .925 sterling silver, and the steel versions start under $35.

That choice is the useful part. The Biohazard Ring costs $32.95 in steel and $52.95 in silver, so you can try a design cheaply, then buy it in silver once you know you'll wear it. The DYT Coffin Ring ($42.95 in steel) has an inner ring that slides out to reveal a hidden coffin. It's a Utah brand, and US sizes run from 3 to 13.

The catch is the return window. You get 14 days, under half of what Clocks and Colours gives you, so order carefully.
bodies.gaboratory:
Gaboratory is the one for collector-grade biker silver, if you can wait for it. Its skull rings start with the Flat Bar Ring (US$223) and pass $2,000 for full-head skulls like the Moon Face Ring ($2,223).

Most pieces are made to order, with delivery quoted at 3 to 10 weeks, and EMS shipping to North America is a flat $38.70. The listed prices are starting prices, and options add to them, so open the ring to see what yours will cost. The shop also runs deep on wallet chains and leather wallets, if you want the whole biker set from one maker.

Need one sooner? The Great Frog makes its pieces in about a week and ships by DHL.
bodies.good-art-hlywd:
Good Art HLYWD is the pick if you want a signet or a band rather than a skull. It makes its silver by hand in its own Los Angeles foundry, and the Cigar Band ($475) takes its shape from a cigar label laid flat.

The Slim Cigar Band ($385) is the cheaper way into the same design. US shipping is free by USPS Priority Mail, and sizes run from US 3.5 to 14, so smaller and larger hands are both covered. Made-to-order pieces take 4 to 6 weeks, while Ready To Ship pieces go out in 3 to 5 business days.

Returns are the weak spot. You get 14 days, for an exchange or store credit only, and a 20% restocking fee comes off the credit. Be sure of your size first.
bodies.clocks-and-colours:
Clocks and Colours is the budget pick for skull rings that come in sterling silver. The Salt & Bone ($69 in steel, $129 in silver) puts a small skull on a bone-shaped band.

It's a Toronto brand, and its silver is hand-carved in Bali. Most rings come in steel or silver, with steel from $69 and silver up to $359. US sizes go from 3 to 16, the widest range on this list, so it's the one to check if other makers stop short of your size. Shipping is free over $100, and you get 30 days to return.

For more than a band, Shadow's Wake ($289) sets a silver raven on a band of ivy and thorns.
bodies.werkstatt-munchen:
Werkstatt:München is the one for hammered, hand-forged silver with a cross on it. Its cross ring forged (€385, about $429) is forged from a bar of silver and winds round the finger twice, so it reads as two rings.

Klaus Lohmeyer, a master gold and silversmith, started it in Munich in 1996, and everything is still handmade in its own atelier. Plain bands like the ring classic round forged start at €175 (about $195). Sizes use French numbers, from 49 to 68, so convert yours before you order.

The extra costs add up for US buyers. Shipping is €43 and import duties are paid on delivery. A return from outside the EU also loses a €50 fee.
bodies.oss:
OSS makes rings that sit somewhere between jewelry and sculpture, handmade in Madrid, and the PSI Ring (€180, about $200) is the easiest way in.

Each piece is made to order in oxidized or black silver. The Centurion Ring (€200, about $223) adds a hand-engraved logo, and the range tops out at €660 (about $735), so it stays well under Werkstatt:München's big pieces. Sizes run from US 4 to 15 across the range. It ships worldwide by UPS, in 4 to 8 business days outside Europe.

Know your size before you buy, because all sales are final. There are no refunds or change-of-mind returns. If that's a deal-breaker, Werkstatt:München's bands come with a 14-day return.
bodies.parts-of-four:
Parts of Four is the art-world take on dark silver, and it's the one pick here that ships free worldwide and pays your import duties. The Crescent Rift Ring in matte sterling silver (€310, about $345) is the entry point.

Evan Sugerman, a Los Angeles-born artist, started it in 2011, and you can visit in Paris. The product names carry codes for the metal, which is worth learning before you browse. MA means matte sterling silver, while 18K and DIA mean gold and diamonds, and that's how prices climb past €12,000.

Returns are an exchange or store credit within 14 days, not a refund. In the US, Atelier in New York and H. Lorenzo in West Hollywood stock it.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with what you'll spend. Hard Jewelry and Clocks and Colours both start under $70, and both let you choose steel or silver. From about $150 to $500 you're into handmade silver. Go to The Great Frog or Bill Wall Leather for skulls and biker motifs, Werkstatt:München or OSS for hammered and sculptural shapes, and Good Art HLYWD for signets and bands. Gaboratory and Parts of Four go well past $1,000 for their big pieces.

Then think about returns. OSS takes nothing back, Good Art gives credit only, and Bill Wall Leather and Clocks and Colours give you 30 days. If you want to hold the ring first, go to The Great Frog in New York or LA.

faqs.a: Richard Stark and his wife, Laurie Lynn Stark. It's a private company with no parent group. Stark founded it in Los Angeles in 1988 with John Bowman and Leonard Kamhout, who both left in 1994.

faqs.q: Where can you buy Chrome Hearts jewelry?
faqs.a: In its own boutiques. The online shop sells underwear, scents and Baccarat crystal, but no jewelry. In the US, there are boutiques in Los Angeles, Malibu, New York, Miami, Las Vegas, Aspen and Honolulu.
faqs.source_query: where to buy chrome hearts jewelry

faqs.a: Mostly in Hollywood, including its silver, gold and diamond pieces, most of its clothing, its leather goods and its furniture. Its eyewear is made mainly in Japan and its fragrances in France.
